Theoretical basis: Replaces missing entries so all records can be used
Suitability for this dataset: Missingness is informative (agent missing: 24.7% vs 39.0% cancelled)
Measured impact: Explicit 'none' / 'Unknown' categories and has_company flag preserve this signal
Risks and limitations: Mean or mode imputation would erase the signal; deletion would bias the class balance

Theoretical basis: Removes repeated records that overweight some patterns
Measured impact: RF F1 0.8235 kept vs 0.8248 removed; base rate falls from 37.1% to 27.6%
Risks and limitations: Deletes real bookings and shifts the base rate; the real problem was evaluation leakage

Theoretical basis: Removes invalid records that contradict domain rules
Measured impact: Negligible effect on metrics; removes impossible bookings
Risks and limitations: Aggressive IQR removal would delete informative extremes (e.g. 91.6% cancel rate)

Theoretical basis: Rescales features to mean 0 and standard deviation 1
Suitability for this dataset: Needed for LR; unscaled LR failed to converge in 3,000 iterations
Measured impact: LR F1 0.7415 to 0.7561; training time 31.46 s to 1.47 s
Risks and limitations: Sensitive to outliers; no benefit for tree models

Theoretical basis: Rescales features to the range 0 to 1
Suitability for this dataset: Heavy tails compress most values into a narrow range
Measured impact: LR F1 0.7535, slightly below standardisation, and slower convergence

Theoretical basis: log(1 + x) compresses large values and reduces right skew
Risks and limitations: Overcorrected adr skew to -3.74; negative values must be clipped

Theoretical basis: Estimates a per-feature power that makes distributions more symmetric
Suitability for this dataset: Best skew reduction in Task 3 (adr 10.53 to 0.41)
Measured impact: LR F1 0.7709, statistically tied with log1p
Risks and limitations: Parameters estimated from data; slower (5.58 s) and less interpretable
Decision: Rejected in favour of simpler log1p

Theoretical basis: Keeps a subset of features to reduce redundancy and noise
Suitability for this dataset: Redundant pairs (V up to 0.88) and unreliable features found in Task 3
Measured impact: All options within 0.003 F1; L1 kept 45 of 110 LR features
Risks and limitations: L1 selection depends on untuned C; may drop one of a correlated pair arbitrarily

Theoretical basis: Derives new features from existing ones
Suitability for this dataset: Stay length and party size are spread across several columns
Measured impact: Enabled removal of component features without loss (Table 4.5)
Risks and limitations: Adds collinearity if originals are kept

Theoretical basis: Projects data onto components retaining maximum variance
Suitability for this dataset: Mixed binary and continuous features; target not considered
Risks and limitations: Variance is not predictive signal; destroys interpretability

Theoretical basis: Creates one binary column per category
Suitability for this dataset: Required for nominal categories in LR; 552 columns with all levels
Measured impact: Rare-level grouping: 110 columns for only 0.004 lower F1
Risks and limitations: Dimensionality explodes for country and agent; sparse input slows RF

Theoretical basis: Replaces each category with its cross-fitted mean target value
Measured impact: RF F1 unchanged (0.8217 vs 0.8220) with 11x faster training
Risks and limitations: Target leakage unless cross-fitted; less useful for LR (F1 0.7630)

Theoretical basis: Creates synthetic minority samples by interpolating between neighbours
Measured impact: No gain; LR training 35x slower; lowest balanced RF F1 (0.8214)
Risks and limitations: 42.24% of synthetic rows had impossible category values

Theoretical basis: Duplicates minority samples until classes are equal
Suitability for this dataset: Minority class already large (35,344 training rows)
Risks and limitations: Exact copies encourage overfitting, as with duplicates

Theoretical basis: Discards majority samples until classes are equal
Measured impact: Highest RF recall (0.8580) but lowest precision (0.8008)

Theoretical basis: Increases the loss penalty for minority-class errors
Suitability for this dataset: Keeps all real data; no synthetic records
Measured impact: Best RF F1 (0.8294); LR recall 0.7357 to 0.8325
Risks and limitations: Lowers precision; best threshold depends on business costs
